title: concept prototype
author: Affectionate_Fact854
selftext:
This is just a small idea that took me 2 hours to set up , documentation , game design , scaffold   
and then i just let the open weight model orchestrate other agents to work 

so they came up with this inspired by [slith.io](http://slith.io)   


i wanted to experience a 3d no axis boundaries version 

no chatgpt, no claude just opencode models used 

rough around the edges but thats what concept prototyping is all about

comments.author: sw3d
comments.body: I'm a big fan of [slither.io](http://slither.io) and this nails it in 3D! Do you have a link? Is the idea to do online multiplayer?

replies.author: Affectionate_Fact854
replies.body:
no link just yet , ill spend another day just making some polish work on this concept and then post a offline version for time being  
  
possibly might look into online but that will take  another phase of first planning how the backend would work to make it secure enough for users :)

replies.author: japherwocky
replies.body: I built out a little [slither.io](http://slither.io) clone in 2D, I was thinking about 3D too, but as a heads up - the multiplayer ended up being much much more complicated than the game itself, reading some writeups of out [slither.io](http://slither.io) implemented it is very helpful.  the bottleneck, surprisingly to me, is the size of the payload going from the server to the client and vice versa;  to get it working with more than single digit users/bots, you have to get into passing the minimum info required in a sort of compressed way.

replies.author: Affectionate_Fact854
replies.body:
Thanks for the heads up with this part , that will be very good starting point!

I think I might try it by maintaining a spacial grid on a server side, and snapshot the changed only, then transmitting deltas between these snapshots 

Not sure yet but reading up docs on how slith.io agar.io and so forth achieved this feat will definitely be a huge help

replies.author: Affectionate_Fact854
replies.body: That's just me guessing at this point as I haven't done the server side research for this prototype yet :0

replies.author: japherwocky
replies.body: I definitely spent at least 10x the time and tokens on the multiplayer bits, but it was extremely interesting, even as a guy who has been doing programming professionally for a while, highly recommend it!

comments.body: Neat, makes me a little nauseous, maybe dim really far orbs to make it readable? (Or leave as is, just a suggestion)

replies.author: Affectionate_Fact854
replies.body:
Yea that is something I'm planning to still also implement, as the idea would be to expand given size of the map 2x , to not cull  distant orbs would anyways ramp up draw calls far to much 

So idea would be 3 layers , hide very far away orbs, mid range would have orbs  dimmed  and possibly merged if visuals is close together , and close being what a person sees clearly. 

This is still the rushed version though 

But thanks:)
